title: Semilinear comparison of localized bilinear functors
statement: Let R,S be commutative rings, C an R-linear and D an S-linear preadditive category [def-weil-linear-category], t in R, s in S, and c:R[1/t] → S[1/s] a ring homomorphism. Let U:C×C → C, V:D×D → D and r:C → D be functors. On their raw scalar localizations [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], let A:L_t(C)×L_t(C) → L_t(C), B:L_s(D)×L_s(D) → L_s(D) and additive T:L_t(C) → L_s(D) have respectively the object maps U,V,r. Assume T(x tensor a)=c(x) tensor r(a). Assume the Hom actions of A and B are represented by maps linear separately over R[1/t] and S[1/s], respectively, and send pairs (x tensor a,y tensor b) to (xy) tensor U(a,b) and (xy) tensor V(a,b). Given a natural isomorphism mu:U followed by r ≅ (r×r) followed by V, there exists a unique natural isomorphism alpha:A followed by T ≅ (T×T) followed by B whose component at (K,N) is heterogeneously equal to Q_D(mu_(K,N)).

proof.text: Construct a normalized natural isomorphism by conjugating localized integral components with the object equalities. Double tensor induction proves naturality from the integral naturality square and coefficient multiplication. For the semilinear composite, postcompose the source bilinear Hom map with the additive scalar functor; precompose the target bilinear Hom map with that functor in both arguments. The pure-tensor map formula and multiplicativity of the coefficient homomorphism identify both comparisons with the normalized integral comparison. Component extensionality proves uniqueness.

theorem bilinearComparison_existsUnique
    {R : Type r} [CommRing R] {S : Type s} [CommRing S]
    {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] [Preadditive C] [Linear R C]
    {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] [Preadditive D] [Linear S D]
    (t : R) (tS : S) (c : Localization.Away t →+* Localization.Away tS)
    (U : C × C ⥤ C) (V : D × D ⥤ D) (r : C ⥤ D)
    (A : ScalarLocalization R C t × ScalarLocalization R C t ⥤ ScalarLocalization R C t)
    (B : ScalarLocalization S D tS × ScalarLocalization S D tS ⥤ ScalarLocalization S D tS)
    (T : ScalarLocalization R C t ⥤ ScalarLocalization S D tS) [T.Additive]
    (hA : ∀ K, A.obj K = ⟨U.obj (K.1.obj, K.2.obj)⟩)
    (hB : ∀ K, B.obj K = ⟨V.obj (K.1.obj, K.2.obj)⟩)
    (hT : ∀ K, T.obj K = ⟨r.obj K.obj⟩)
    (mT : ∀ (K K' : C) (a : K ⟶ K') (x : Localization.Away t),
      HEq (T.map (x ⊗ₜ[R] a : ScalarLocalization.mk K ⟶ ScalarLocalization.mk K'))
        (c x ⊗ₜ[S] r.map a))
    (mA : ∀ (K K' N N' : ScalarLocalization R C t),
      ∃ β : (K ⟶ K') →ₗ[Localization.Away t] (N ⟶ N') →ₗ[Localization.Away t]
          (A.obj (K, N) ⟶ A.obj (K', N')),
        (∀ a b, A.map (Prod.mkHom a b) = β a b) ∧
        ∀ (a : K.obj ⟶ K'.obj) (b : N.obj ⟶ N'.obj) (x y : Localization.Away t),
          HEq (β (x ⊗ₜ[R] a) (y ⊗ₜ[R] b)) ((x * y) ⊗ₜ[R] U.map (Prod.mkHom a b)))
    (mB : ∀ (K K' N N' : ScalarLocalization S D tS),
      ∃ β : (K ⟶ K') →ₗ[Localization.Away tS] (N ⟶ N') →ₗ[Localization.Away tS]
          (B.obj (K, N) ⟶ B.obj (K', N')),
        (∀ a b, B.map (Prod.mkHom a b) = β a b) ∧
        ∀ (a : K.obj ⟶ K'.obj) (b : N.obj ⟶ N'.obj) (x y : Localization.Away tS),
          HEq (β (x ⊗ₜ[S] a) (y ⊗ₜ[S] b)) ((x * y) ⊗ₜ[S] V.map (Prod.mkHom a b)))
    (μ : U ⋙ r ≅ r.prod r ⋙ V) :
    ∃! α : A ⋙ T ≅ T.prod T ⋙ B,
      ∀ K, HEq (α.hom.app K)
        ((ScalarLocalization.localization S D tS).map (μ.hom.app (K.1.obj, K.2.obj)))
